casestudies.title: NAVIS
casestudies.subtitle: ENEL 500 — Engineering Capstone · Fall 2025 – Winter 2026
casestudies.overview: NAVIS is a smart navigation glasses system built for low-emission travellers who rely on phones for directions. The system delivers real-time GPS guidance through an OLED lens display attached to wearable glasses and bone-conduction audio. No hands. No screen-checking. Built with accessible components and fully open-source documented for future teams.
casestudies.problem: Non-motorized travellers (cyclists, pedestrians, mobility aid users) often rely on phones for navigation, which requires looking away from the path and can be unsafe. NAVIS offloads navigation cues to a wearable display, with the companion app serving as the configuration and control hub.

design.title: UX Design
points: Designed the companion app interface in Figma

engineering.title: Development
points: Real-time BLE connectivity with nRF52840 MCU
Agile sprints with bi-weekly reviews in Jira

process.title: Glanceability
process.description: App used while in motion — UI needed to communicate status at a glance.

process.title: BLE States
process.description: Clear feedback for connecting, connected, and disconnected hardware states.

process.title: Cross-team
process.description: Coordinated design decisions with hardware and firmware teams throughout.

process.title: Iteration
process.description: Designs updated as firmware capabilities evolved over the project timeline.

casestudies.title: PeerHive
casestudies.subtitle: Designathon · November 2025 · 5.5 hours
casestudies.overview: PeerHive is a social discovery platform designed to help students find mentors and mentees based on shared interests and skill proficiency. Built end-to-end in 5.5 hours at a Designathon, the project challenged our team to move fast without skipping the fundamentals.
casestudies.problem: Students often struggle to find the right mentorship connections — existing platforms are either too broad or require institutional gatekeeping. The prompt asked us to design a solution that made meaningful peer connections more accessible and low-friction.

primary.title: Primary Research
points: Identified pain points with existing discovery tools
Mapped motivations for seeking / offering mentorship

secondary.title: Secondary Research
points: Reviewed platforms students currently use (LinkedIn, Discord)

process.title: Discover
process.description: User surveys + competitive review to define the problem space before touching Figma.

process.title: Define
process.description: Synthesized research into a clear problem statement and user needs.

process.title: Ideate
process.description: Rapid sketching and team alignment on core flows and features.

process.title: Prototype
process.description: High-fidelity prototype in HTML/CSS delivered within the time limit.

outcome.text: Placed 1st in the Experienced Track. The research-first approach — defining the problem before opening design tools — was a core reason the final prototype felt cohesive and user-grounded despite the time constraint.

casestudies.title: FanFest Expo
casestudies.subtitle: CPSC 481 — Human-Computer Interaction I · Winter 2025
casestudies.overview: FanFest Expo is a convention navigation system designed to help attendees find panels, vendors, and events across a large venue. The project was built for CPSC 481 (Human-Computer Interaction I), applying HCI principles and WCAG accessibility standards throughout the entire design and development process.
casestudies.problem: Convention-goers often feel overwhelmed navigating large, multi-hall events with dense schedules and limited wayfinding. The goal was to design an intuitive navigation tool that works across mobile and desktop, reduces cognitive load, and remains accessible to all users.

process.title: Research
process.description: Studied existing event apps and identified usability gaps through HCI literature and heuristic evaluation.

process.title: Wireframes
process.description: Low and mid-fidelity wireframes for both mobile and desktop layouts.

process.title: Accessibility
process.description: Applied WCAG standards: contrast ratios, keyboard navigation, semantic HTML, ARIA labels.

process.title: Implementation
process.description: Responsive Next.js front end deployed via Vercel, matching the high-fidelity Figma prototypes.

keyDecisions.title: Mobile-First Layout
points: Convention attendees are on the go

keyDecisions.title: Accessibility First
points: Semantic HTML for screen reader support

casestudies.title: Cartify
casestudies.subtitle: SENG 513 — Web-Based Systems · Fall 2025
casestudies.overview: Cartify is a full-stack marketplace platform that combines product buying and renting into a single, cohesive experience. As team lead, I owned both the product design and GitLab collaboration, designing high-fidelity prototypes for mobile and desktop before any code was written.
casestudies.problem: Users who want to buy or rent products are forced to use separate platforms, creating friction and fragmenting the experience. Cartify aimed to unify both models under one interface without overwhelming the user with complexity.

design.title: Design
points: Led all UI/UX design in Figma
User flows for buy, rent, and listing flows

engineering.title: Engineering
points: Project lead — managed GitLab and sprints

process.title: Define
process.description: Mapped out core user journeys: browsing, buying, renting, and listing.

process.title: Prototype
process.description: High-fidelity Figma prototypes for mobile and desktop before development began.

process.title: Build
process.description: Full-stack implementation in React, Node.js, and MySQL with Docker.

process.title: Iterate
process.description: Adjusted designs based on what surfaced during development and peer review.
